barCharacter: Vera Oberlin (top of the hierarchy, never asks permission, transactional, clipped; the corpus holds only 9 Vera lines, so the bar set is padded with the 3 narrator lines that carry her comedy). BAR 12: "Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you!" / "You'd be willing to cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right?" / "Right. Now." / "Ugh, it's such a chore being this beautiful all the time. How am I ever going to get rid of him?" / "only [drinks] four things: scotch, red wine, the tears of [her] enemies, and straight up poison" / "I need a way to get ahead of the pack. And since you're SUCH a good advisor..." / "Girl, we need to have a little talk about feminism. You, back me up on this. Tell her she doesn't need to poison herself for the sake of a man." / "Now I just need to find a way to reinforce the superiority of the Cools over the Un-Cools." / "Come on, think of something! You're my most trusted advisor!" / Narrator: "You see Vera at the mirror, attempting to tame her hair with a cattle prod." / Narrator: "Whoa. You know this is a serious situation if it's causing Vera to show empathy." / Narrator: "You turn around to find Vera staring at you. This often happens, but for some reason it's not a death stare this time." OURS 12: "Nav, I muted the moon landing. I can mute you." / "Brock, the neighbours will complain. I own the neighbours." / "Brock. You're too loud for my hours. I'm changing my hours." / "Quill, every word costs me a second. You owe me a week." / "Too big for radio. I'll make radio bigger." / "Vex, that's a horoscope, and I write those." / "Brock, you'd be wonderful at seven a.m. I don't exist then." / "Dash, I've lost the hour. I am the clock." / "I heard clapping under that. One pair of hands." / "Tilly, I've turned you up twice. I'm at the top." / "Don't breathe. The mic picks up hope." / "Quill, a man rang to ask if you're all right." VOICE (bar): cover the names and the radio nouns and Vesper's shape (flat statement, full stop, short drop) is the same shape Maximilian and Crumb use; "I own the neighbours" and "calm is my job" are concierge lines with a different noun. Vera's sentences carry her even without topic: the "Right?" tag, the repeated-word fake-out, the player as "advisor", the complaint-as-boast. CONSTRUCTION (tie): our best 12 are tighter than Vera's set, which includes functional prompt lines (#46, #50) and a 28-word lecture; but six of our 12 lean on one move (I control X, so Y), and two of the best (moon landing, changing my hours) are lifted straight from the persona brief's own examples. QUOTABLE (bar): Vera assumes you will hide a murder; that is a clip. Vesper's best are a knowing smile. Her stakes are a milkman, bins, the licence people, a pigeon man; Monster Prom runs high stakes with low sincerity, and ours runs cosy stakes with dry sincerity. If both ran tonight, Vera is the better-written character.
genericLines: Crumb, was that a joke? Neither of us knows.
Crumb, say it like you'd miss me.
Vex, guess what I want. Get it wrong on purpose.
Vex, tell me one thing about yourself that nobody asked for.
Prince, I still don't believe you. Stay anyway.
Nav, you didn't shout once. Come here.
Nav, calm is my job. Get your own.
Crumb, dry is my department. Yours is closed.
Prince, I opened that with gloves on.
Act surprised, Vex, for the listeners.
Vex, for the record, I worked this out myself.
Vex, you guessed me all night. Nobody guesses me twice.
Vex, you knew how tonight ends. Now you do.
Tilly, I'm ending this call. You never would.
Brock, say it at that volume forever.
No maybe in that. I'll keep it.
That's the most honest thing on medium wave tonight.
I've broadcast through a flood. That was a puddle.
I got this letter by telegram, and replied stop.
Quiet now. This is the part I like.
Same time tomorrow. I'll be here. I'm always here.
Your worst habit. I'll find it in a week anyway. Save us the week.
Apologise for our first fight. It hasn't happened. I'm owed it anyway.
{name} handled my ex. Nobody handles my ex.
{name} stopped at three. Nobody stops at three.
{name} pitched a rival. I'm keeping the pitcher.
{name} sold me a flaw. I'm keeping it. No refunds.
{name}'s apology is accepted. The fight is pencilled in.
I'm hungry. Neither of you should have done that. You both did.
Two of you planned my night. Nobody plans my night. Apparently.
You both did exactly as you were told. Nobody does that here.
I've been called wonderful twice tonight. I'm checking which one meant it.
Two vocabularies tonight. I understood a third of each.
Neither of you said maybe once. I noticed. I always notice.
Two callers made themselves the joke. I laughed at the right one.
Two of you said something frightened. Nobody hung up. Least of all me.
You were both unkind about the others. The others have gone. Good.
{name}, the word that cut you tonight was maybe.
{name}, somebody kept a scoreboard of themselves tonight. I read it.
{name}, it rhymed or it didn't. That was the whole night.
{name}, the other callers were the subject tonight. That decided it.
{name}, somebody kept making themselves the punchline. It settled things.
{name}, I kept score of who asked about me. That's the reason.
{name}, my stomach decided this one. Think about what you fed it.
{name}, tonight came down to a timetable. You know if you brought one.
{name}, nice things were said about me tonight. I weighed every one.
{name}, somebody did sums at me tonight. Sums lose.
{name}, some answers tonight never arrived. I waited. That's your reason.
{name}, the length of a line decided this. Measure yours on the bus.
{name}, I needed a dictionary tonight. That's your clue.
{name}, one caller tonight sounded frightened. That was the verdict.
Sorry, Tilly. See? It's easy. Goodnight.
Nav, you kept telling me where to go. I'm already there. Always.
The heating's been broken since seventy-three. I'm telling you because nobody else asks.
Off mic: I'd decided before the second round. I like watching them work for it.

biggestGap: Her cringe and unsure lines insult by comparison to cosy British radio ephemera (bins, the licence people, a double-glazing advert, the pigeon man, the milkman, the raffle), so the period prop is the joke and her status is not, which breaks her own brief.
